items.title: Josiah "Cie" Frazier Interview
items.q: And Sam, he played with Kid René and part with Louis Armstrong

ctx.x: Your younger brother, you still have another young...

Yeah, Simon Fraser. Yeah, he's living with my second oldest sister, yeah. Yeah. I think it's in the 26th... No, the 2500 Dumaine Street. He was in... That's the one... He allowed him how to play the piano to, Simon Fraser, yeah. And... Let's see, we have... Like I first said, I started... Now, my oldest brother, and Paul Barberin, another old drummer, they all started by Amarico's Woodyard on North Ramport Street years ago. And Sam, he played with Kid René and part with Louis Armstrong, before Louis ever think…
Did you...when you took up drums, did you have any lessons? Did your father help you or any...

items.title: Josiah 'Cie' Frazier Interview, 1972-01-19
items.q: And we took, we rehearsed for about a whole week, not every evening, to get all the record numbers like Lewis played.

ctx.x: And the Pack House that was located on the court had the restaurant and ball and pool table downstairs. They called it, they was run by this fella by the name of Faubacher. And this fella, Bebe, William Ridgely's brother, he was the manager of the place. I think I don't know, remember his name? His first name? Yeah, his first name was Bebe Ridgely, his first name, he was a big tall, brown skin, heavy built man. But he was the manager of that place there, I can't think of his first name. But all I can tell you,…
What's the name of that band?
